title: Federal Government Scraps Mistral: AI Framework Agreement with SAP Off the Table for Now
source_used: Basic Tutorials (relaying Die Welt, Politico and Golem)
key_facts: The German federal government has for now abandoned plans for an AI framework agreement with France's Mistral and the software company SAP.
A spokesperson for the Federal Ministry for Digital Affairs confirmed to Politico that the government has no procurement plans involving Mistral; Die Welt also reported the withdrawal.
The ministry said the collaboration will be developed independently by the companies, and left open whether the project is scrapped or may return in modified form.
Germany and France presented the partnership in November 2025: AI-powered administration software for agencies and digital agents for civil servants and citizens.
Neither the German government nor Mistral gave reasons; SAP said its own collaboration with Mistral continues unchanged.
Golem points to possible factors: the merger of Aleph Alpha and Cohere creating another public-sector AI provider based in Germany, and doubts about Mistral's models.

Ecosia chief executive Christian Kroll told Politico his company is leaving Mistral, saying its models lag about a year behind; Mistral co-founder Guillaume Lample pointed to the new Mistral Large 4, which independent tests rank behind top OpenAI, Anthropic and Kimi models.
quote_evidence: The German federal government has, for the time being, abandoned plans for an AI framework agreement with the French company Mistral and the software giant SAP.
The ministry left open whether the project will be completely scrapped or revived in a modified form.
Neither the German government nor Mistral commented on the reasons for the withdrawal.
why_it_matters_hint: A flagship German-French plan for European-built AI in public offices is on hold, and no reason has been given.
event_date: Reported 12 Oct 2026 (the dates of the Die Welt and Politico originals are not stated); partnership announced Nov 2025
notes: Die Welt, Politico and Golem not opened; text read on Basic Tutorials, which credits them. The 'possible factors' are Golem's reading, not an official reason. Ecosia leaving Mistral was carried in our 9 Oct 2026 edition (POLITICO Europe, 6 Oct 2026). Basic Tutorials' closing comment is opinion and is not used as fact.
